summary: I codes the sucker as subject; III can code either the nurse or an external arranger as agent. 81/71 ʕal tərto and 81/96 mi Qaračiyayo distinguish milk-source/nurse from the arranging agent.
Repeated nursing in III Infectum-wa is securely attested in human and animal contexts. Add the missing box without converting ordinary omitted-object nursing into a lactation sense.
The episode in 94/192 separates wanting, prevention and the cow's mistaken belief; the same Infectum form does not imply that milk was actually taken.
Retain the edition's Nund typo, milk paraphrases and parenthetical Lämmer; semantic analysis and editorial questions do not license new translations.
Confirm root, -ən ending and physical operation of gmaṣən (JTM 2.5/11): suction, squeezing, straining or pouring off? No new sense is published pending this.
Check mamṣówalle in MAC NE Shangali Pangali/2: nursing the kids versus the English milk them, and the exact suffix segmentation.
Does plural -nne in MAC NE interview 1/27 generalise to babies despite the singular brother frame?
Does absolute mamiṣowa in 81/95 denote lactation or nursing with an omitted child?
In Talay 1/243 are a ʕwonaṯṯe the nursing mothers or the young animals allowed to suck? Do not infer the answer from supplied Lämmer.
Confirm PrS 78/60 as the local counterpart of inherited prs 229/9 before treating its expanded context as a separate example.
Suction includes blood, milk, venom and food from a horn, with substance objects or m-sources; medical equipment does not itself create a new sense.
